units.source_text: Sexual exclusivity got much more important once agriculture, property and inheritance entered the picture.
units.output_text: Monogamy, particularly the sexual aspect of it, has become much more important since agriculture, and the advent of property and inheritance.

units.source_text: By the Industrial Revolution, the strict version was everywhere, with law and social pressure behind it.
units.output_text: By the Industrial Revolution it was being universally enforced in some strict form, often through both law and social pressure.

units.source_text: Plenty of tribal cultures have been much looser about what could happen outside a primary partnership, including other sexual or emotional relationships.
units.output_text: Prior to that, there were many tribal cultures that were far more relaxed about allowing sexual and even emotional contact with others outside of the primary partnership. I believe the term "social monogamy" has been coined to describe this.

There’s a term for some of that: social monogamy.

I took exclusivity further than that.
units.output_text: I took this idea to its logical extreme.

units.source_text: B. wanted to marry me, but I was still attracted to other women, and somehow I decided that meant I shouldn’t marry her yet.
units.output_text: I told B, when she told me she wanted to marry me, that although I wanted to marry her, I was still sexually attracted to other women.

units.source_text: I told her, “It’s not fair of me to commit to you if I’m still attracted to other women, so before I do, let me see if I can fix that.”
